# A menu given its tree store as a class or config opens its submenus

Owned: a leaf of #21367 until its lock, Sun 22 Nov 18:00 CET.

## Context

Defect-note `e71871ff`, reproduced on `dev` 5a3cb4de67 at 1024 × 768: in `examples/menu/tree`, a click on File removes the menu from the stage. Before the click, `#neo-menu-list-1` holds File, Edit, View and About; after it, no `.neo-menu-list` is in the DOM, and the console holds no error.

## The Problem

`menu.List#beforeSetStore` recognises a tree store only as an instance: `value instanceof TreeStore` (`src/menu/List.mjs:334`). The example passes the class, `store: MainStore`. The tree store then becomes the level's own store, and `sourceStore` stays null. It still looks right: a `TreeStore`'s items are its visible rows, and with every parent collapsed those are the four roots. `hasChildren()` then falls back to nested `items` (`:612-619`), so every parent reads as a leaf. A click on File takes the leaf branch of `onKeyDownEnter()` (`:789-794`), and `hideOnLeafItemClick` unmounts the root.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: `menu.List#beforeSetStore`'s JSDoc, "the tree store is kept as `sourceStore` and this level receives its own flat store holding exactly the records it renders" (`src/menu/List.mjs:326-327`), with `@param {Object|Neo.data.Store|Neo.data.TreeStore} value`. Its parent `list.Base#beforeSetStore` takes an instance, a class or a config through `ClassSystemUtil.beforeSetInstance(value, Store)` (`src/list/Base.mjs`).

- #17839's trap holds: submenus share the root's tree store and must never destroy it. They receive it as an instance (`:593-597`).
- An instance handed in stays its owner's: `menu.List#destroy` only unregisters from `sourceStore` (`:466-472`).
- The source is bound once, in `onConstructed()` (`:765-782`): a store set later reaches neither the level nor the listeners.

## The Fix

- `src/menu/List.mjs`
  - `beforeSetStore`: a class or config is built first, through `ClassSystemUtil.beforeSetInstance(value, Store)`, so a tree store is recognised however it arrives.
  - A tree store this menu built is its own, and `destroy()` destroys it after the submenus. One handed in as an instance stays its owner's.
  - A store that replaces another after construction retires the old cascade and its listeners, releases an old source the menu built, and fills the root from the new source (`afterSetStore`).
- `test/playwright/unit/menu/ListTreeStore.spec.mjs`: arms for the class and the config form, for ownership, and for a live replacement.

## Decision Record impact

none

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: In `examples/menu/tree`, a click on File keeps the menu and opens File's submenu (New, Open, Save).
- [ ] AC-2: A tree store passed as an instance, a class or a config drives the same levels: `hasChildren()` reads `isLeaf`, and a parent opens its submenu.
- [ ] AC-3: A menu destroys a tree store it built from a class or config, never one passed in as an instance, and never from a submenu. A store that replaces the source after construction re-derives the root, retires the open cascade and releases only a source the menu built.

## Out of Scope

- `hasChildren()`'s nested-`items` fallback for a plain store: it is the classic API.
- The example's catalog record and cover (#21142, the renewal under #21367).

## Avoided Traps

- **Passing an instance in the example.** It hides the engine gap for the next consumer, and the example would then own a store nobody destroys.
- **`autoDestroyStore` for the source.** It governs the level store; reading it for the source would destroy instances other owners share.
